subjects: SUBJECT COMPOSITION CONTRACT: Return compatibleComposition for EVERY candidate with nonempty allowed-value lists for support, backdrop, pattern, depth and contextDensity. These constraints describe physically and semantically natural presentations, not artistic preferences. Support values are none, simple-plane, material-surface, environment; use the provided statistics for the remaining stable facet values. A parked or driving wheeled vehicle requires ground contact (environment); never allow none merely because it could be redrawn as floating. Hanging objects can use none inside an environment when naturally suspended. Ordinary airborne objects can use none. Keep compatibleCategories consistent with ALL compatibleComposition facets. The application matches category and every required composition facet together. A final concept is only the narrative of the selected ten subjects: never describe primary/reserve roster bookkeeping in the concept or roles. On repair preserve the valid story and subjects; correct incompatible candidates or compatibility declarations using the rejection evidence rather than redesigning everything.
details: ART CONTRACT DETAILS: Return lighting and materialTreatment for each variant, in addition to paletteRhythm and the ten card descriptions. Resolve actual light direction, softness, highlight character, shadow direction, fill and brightness from the original rendering references. Resolve concrete treatment for the selected materials while preserving canonical rules. Apply these choices consistently. Every slot must remain physically natural for its assigned support; report contradictions through the descriptions, never describe a grounded object as floating to appease metadata. Treat the fixed ten slots as the final roster, not primary/reserve candidates. Review feedback may correct the shared lighting, material treatment and descriptions; those fields are used by the compiler.
review: PLANNING REVIEW BOUNDARY: The proposed set is a persistent semantic/art contract. Stable reference IDs belong there; stage-specific attachment numbers MUST NOT be embedded in its text. The separate numbered input manifest supplied with THIS review binds each image to its stable ID, category and purpose. Final generation receives its own complete input manifest after per-card retrieval. Do not reject the plan for missing image numbers inside its artContract or per-card reference selection that has not happened yet. Review the concrete subject/slot physics, shared resolved lighting/material treatment and image-brief visual completeness. An ordinary surface or ground contact is required only for a subject that naturally needs it; a hanging or airborne subject can be unsupported within a category-4 environment. Never require all category-4 objects to stand on the ground.
take: Use canonical rendering, light and material cues; category metadata identifies composition examples. The final per-card request selects its own matching-category references.
ignore: Do not copy reference subjects, interface, typography or exact layouts.
